title: CLI-written model attachments are stored as ready and cannot be downloaded
description:
Found during the relevance cyclotron sandbox run (PPY-ac39d8).

Evidence: src/papyrus_content/model_attachments.py builds every Python-written ModelAttachment with status 'ready' (build_json_model_payload_attachment and friends). completeModelAttachmentUpload stores the status it is given (amplify/functions/model-attachment-upload/handler.ts), and createModelAttachmentDownload refuses anything not 'active' ('ModelAttachment ... is ready, not active.'). So research packet metadata written by 'papyrus research apply', and the cyclotron status snapshot written by the decide-relevance sweep, cannot be read back through the download API (the References tab's status strip, research-packet proposal intake). Browser uploads default to 'active' and are unaffected.

```gherkin
Feature: Attachments the CLI writes can be read back
  Scenario: A JSON payload the CLI uploads is active
    Given a JSON payload built by the Python authoring tools
    When it is uploaded and completed
    Then its stored status is active
```

Done when Python-written attachments default to 'active' and a spec covers it. Records already stored as 'ready' are rewritten when their payloads are written again.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Fixed on fix/PPY-296a7f-cli-attachments-active: build_json_model_payload_attachment (and every Python payload built through it) defaults to status active; spec procedures/newsroom/tests/test_model_attachment_status.py (2). Verified in sandbox ppy-6b4094: re-applying a research packet rewrote its metadata attachment as active and proposal intake then registered 30 pending references (before the fix it read 0 because the download API refused the 'ready' attachment). No new pytest/BDD failures.

right_now_summary: CLI-written attachments now default to active and can be downloaded.
